subject: Failure analysis and customer debrief: May 22 multi-region inference degradation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Failure analysis and customer debrief: May 22 multi-region inference degradation

Hi Helen / Rajesh,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our investigation into the degradation you saw on May 22 (multi-region inference latency spikes affecting a subset of requests). Below is a concise customer-facing debrief with the key findings, timeline, and what we are doing to make sure this doesn't recur. We attached a short technical appendix for your SREs.

Summary (TL;DR)
- What happened: An internal cache eviction storm combined with a gradual kernel fallback caused increased tail latency for requests routed to our eu-west-1 and us-east-1 pools.
- Impact: ~12% of FinBase requests experienced latency > 2s for a 42-minute window; no data loss or consistency issues were observed.
- Root cause: A recently deployed autoscaling tweak inadvertently reduced the grace window for KV-cache population during node termination, which, under a correlated VM drain pattern, triggered repeated cold-cache lookups and a fallback to a more conservative execution kernel.

Timeline (high level)
- 2027-05-22 10:43 UTC — First internal alerts: elevated p50/p95 on inference routes serving FinBase.
- 2027-05-22 10:46 UTC — Increased error budgets observed; routing system began shifting traffic as expected.
- 2027-05-22 10:54 UTC — Kernel fallback path triggered for some nodes; tail latency rose sharply.
- 2027-05-22 11:25 UTC — Mitigation: we applied a temporary routing cap and extended cache population grace window. Latency returned to baseline by 11:35 UTC.

Immediate corrective actions we've completed
- Rolled back the autoscaling grace-window change across affected clusters (complete).
- Deployed a mitigant that stabilizes kernel selection under transient cold-cache conditions (complete).
- Added targeted alerts to detect correlated node drains and cache-population regressions (complete).

Planned follow-ups (next 30 days)
- Engineering (Marcus): full postmortem with implementation of permanent guardrails around autoscaling triggers (ETA: 2027-06-04).
- Performance (Marissa): broader regression tests across sequence-length distributions to ensure kernel fallback thresholds are safe for your workload (ETA: 2027-06-07).
- Account/CS (Naomi): scheduling a 30-min technical review with your SREs to walk the appendix and answer questions (proposed times below).

Attachments: 20270523_finbase_rca.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB) — contains the full timeline, logs excerpt, and remediation plan.
Also attached: query_logs_excerpt.txt — sample queries highlighting affected pathways.

Proposed times for a short sync: 2027-05-24 15:00 UTC or 2027-05-25 09:00 UTC. Please let me know which slot works and I will send a calendar invite.

Thank you again for raising this and for working through it with us. We recognize the impact and are prioritizing the permanent fixes.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Helen — good questions, thanks. Quick answers inline, full details in the attached appendix: 

1) Client-side retries: we did not count retries toward the impacted percentage. The 12% figure is computed from successful first-attempt requests that had tail latency > 2s. Retries were rare for this window (<<1%).

2) Affected endpoints/model variants: primarily the convai_v2 and rerank-lite variants served from our shared serving pool; I included the endpoint list in the PDF appendix and a short CSV in the logs excerpt.

Additional notes:
- The kernel fallback was triggered when the KV cache miss-rate exceeded 78% for a node within a 2-minute window — that threshold was hit in nodes undergoing concurrent termination.
- We have attached a trimmed log sample (query_logs_excerpt.txt) with request ids for your SREs to correlate.

I've scheduled the sync for 2027-05-24 15:00 UTC and sent a calendar invite to all. The invite includes the drive link with the appendix: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1abcRCAsign

Agenda for the sync (30 minutes):
- 5m: quick recap and impact metrics

- 10m: Q&A and next steps (including SLA credit / escalation path if you want to discuss)
- 5m: confirm follow-up owners and dates

If you'd like, Marcus can walk the kernel selection changes and Marissa will cover regression test scope.

Best,
Naomi

Helen / Naomi — adding a couple of technical clarifications from the engineering team:

- Permanent guardrail plan: we will implement a requirement that any autoscaling grace-window change must go through a canary phase where KV cache population behavior is validated against a synthetic workload that mimics FinBase traffic. Goal: prevent a repeat of correlated cache-population regressions.
- Timeline: this work is in sprint and targeted for completion by 2027-06-04. We'll run the canary for at least 48 hours and share the canary metrics with FinBase SREs.
- Risk mitigation: we are also hardening the kernel selection logic so that under high miss-rate transient conditions we prefer a degraded-but-stable kernel rather than frequent kernel switching, which was amplifying latency variance during the incident.

I'll be on the sync tomorrow and can walk the canary plan.

—Marcus
